subject.title: Add Gee runtime ownership envelope for OpenClaw

question: Should OpenClaw support a generic external host-runtime ownership contract for auth, tools, compaction, and failover, or should Gee remain an external plugin integration using existing seams?
rationale: The PR creates a new cross-cutting product and security boundary rather than repairing an established behavior, and repository policy reserves owner-specific provider/auth/default policy for the owning plugin.

options.title: Define a generic hosted-runtime seam
options.body: Sponsor a narrowly documented plugin/SDK contract, then require this work to move Gee-specific behavior out of core before it lands.

options.title: Keep Gee external
options.body: Decline a new core ownership mode and implement any supported Gee integration through existing plugin and runtime APIs.

options.title: Pause the proposal
options.body: Close or defer the branch until an owner specifies the supported host-runtime product boundary and upgrade contract.

recommendation.title: Define a generic hosted-runtime seam
recommendation.body: Sponsor a narrowly documented plugin/SDK contract, then require this work to move Gee-specific behavior out of core before it lands.

likelyOwner.reason: The required decision spans OpenClaw’s core/plugin architecture and provider ownership boundary.
